exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.form_cue: Sit tall. Draw chin straight back (double chin). Feel a stretch at the base of the skull. Do NOT tilt your head down.
exercises.why: Your daily insurance policy. Chin tucks open the C5-6 foramen and keep the C6 nerve root decompressed — this is what keeps the pins and needles from coming back.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Flexion
exercises.form_cue: Press your forehead gently into your palm. Resist — don't let the head move. Hold 5-7 sec.
exercises.why: Maintains deep cervical flexor strength so your neck can tolerate the loading you're about to add in the gym.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Extension
exercises.form_cue: Press the back of your head into your palm. Resist evenly. Hold 5-7 sec.
exercises.why: Balances the front-of-neck work and supports the C5-6 segment under load.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeezes
exercises.form_cue: Pinch your shoulder blades together and DOWN. Hold 5 sec. Don't shrug toward your ears.
exercises.why: Sets up the postural foundation for every pulling exercise — a strong upper back protects the cervical spine when you lift.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Tilt your head away from the tight side, gentle hand overpressure. STOP if you feel any radiating pain. Focus on the LEFT side.
exercises.why: Releases the dominant left-sided tension. Keep it gentle now that symptoms have calmed — this is maintenance, not rescue.

exercises.name: Isometric Wrist Extension Hold
exercises.form_cue: Forearm on a table, palm down, wrist over the edge. Hold a light weight and keep the wrist still in a slightly extended position for 30 sec. No pain.
exercises.why: Isometric holds reduce tendon pain and prime the tendon for the heavier loading to come. The safest first step back into elbow strength.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extensions
exercises.form_cue: Forearm on table, wrist over edge, palm down. Lift the wrist with your other hand, then SLOWLY lower it under control (3 sec). Start light (1-2 kg).
exercises.why: The gold standard for tennis elbow. Slow eccentric loading remodels and strengthens the common extensor tendon at the lateral epicondyle.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Straighten the arm, palm up. Use your other hand to press the fingers back toward you.
exercises.why: Balances the forearm and reduces tension through the elbow joint.

exercises.name: Forearm Supination / Pronation
exercises.form_cue: Hold a light dumbbell by one end (or a hammer). Slowly rotate the forearm palm-up then palm-down. Elbow stays pinned to your side.
exercises.why: Strengthens the rotators that support the lateral epicondyle and prepares your grip for pulling work.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.form_cue: Feet shoulder-width on the platform. Push through your heels, stop just short of locking out. Keep your head resting on the pad — never crane it forward.
exercises.why: Rebuilds quad and glute strength with zero load on your spine or neck — the safest way to start reloading your legs.

exercises.name: Goblet Box Squat
exercises.form_cue: Hold a light dumbbell at your chest. Sit back to a box or bench, then stand tall. Eyes forward, neck neutral — do NOT look up.
exercises.why: Re-grooves the squat with the load in front, which keeps your torso upright and your neck relaxed. The box sets a safe, consistent depth.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
exercises.form_cue: Lie face-down on an incline bench. Row dumbbells toward your ribs, squeezing shoulder blades down and back. Keep your chest on the pad. Straps OK if grip bothers the elbow.
exercises.why: Builds the upper-back strength that holds your head over your shoulders — and the bench support removes all strain from your neck.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.form_cue: Set the seat so the handles sit at mid-chest. Press smoothly. Keep your shoulders down — don't shrug toward your ears.
exercises.why: Pressing strength without the neck-and-shoulder stabilising demand of a free-weight bench. Ideal for phase one.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.form_cue: Rope at face height. Pull toward your forehead, elbows high, squeeze the rear delts. Light weight, slow and controlled.
exercises.why: Directly trains the postural muscles of the upper back and neck — one of the best exercises for long-term cervical health.

exercises.name: DB Romanian Deadlift (light)
exercises.form_cue: Soft knees, hinge at the hips, slide the dumbbells down your thighs until you feel a hamstring stretch. Flat back, neutral neck. Stand up by squeezing your glutes.
exercises.why: Teaches the hip hinge that protects your lower back and builds the glutes and hamstrings you'll need for running later.

exercises.name: Dead Bugs
exercises.form_cue: On your back, arms up, knees at 90°. Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back pressed flat.
exercises.why: Deep core stability with zero compression on the neck or spine — the foundation for bracing under heavier loads.
